item.title: Computer Applications Frontiers: Opportunities, Challenges, Technologies and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Xiaoou Ding, Harbin Institute of Technology

Kaiyu Li, Wilfrid Laurier University

This special issue focuses on advanced computer application technologies such as AI, Big Data, Large Models, Blockchain, IoT, Cloud Computing, 5G, and Digital Twins, and their integration across various industries. A key challenge is building efficient, secure, and intelligent systems that enable interoperability between industrial equipment, information systems, business processes, and enterprise services.

The issue seeks original research and review papers that address technical challenges and explore how intelligent methods and self-adaptive models can provide solutions relevant to dynamic engineering environments, particularly in fields like transportation and environmental engineering where conditions change rapidly.

The special issue aims to assess the current state of the art in using advanced computer applications to tackle complex interoperability challenges, identify knowledge gaps, and propose future research directions for both academia and industry.

Appel publié par Expert Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Frontier Technology Applications of intelligent systems, including intelligent Energy, Manufacturing, Transportation, Finance, etc.
  • Artificial intelligence technologies, including Large Models, Deep Learning, Feature Extraction and Selection
  • Pervasive Computing and Environmental Intelligence
  • Robotics and Intelligent Systems, including Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Biometric Recognition
  • Brain-Computer Interfaces
  • Data Science and Big Data Technologies, including System Frameworks, Data Preprocessing, Visualization, Mining, and Privacy
  • Cybersecurity Technologies including Future Grid Architectures, Distributed Computing, Cybersecurity, Mobile Communications
  • Internet of Things and Sensor Networks
  • Cloud Computing and Service Computing
  • Smart Healthcare and Agriculture
  • AI and Machine Learning for the Design, Optimization, and Modeling of RF, Microwave, Millimeter-Wave Circuits, Components, and Antennas
  • Intelligent Design and Engineering of Reconfigurable RF Devices, Smart Antennas, and Next-Generation Wireless Communication Systems

Timeline

  • August 20, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Smart systems and the governance of sociotechnical transformation
item.content:encoded:
Wanhao Zhang, Norwegian University of Science and Technology

Younghoon Chang, University of Nottingham Ningbo China

Sameer Kumar, University of Malaya

Smart systems are increasingly embedded in everyday life across homes, workplaces, healthcare, education and public services, functioning not just as tools but as sociotechnical arrangements that shape human behaviour and institutional practices. This special issue explores how these systems integrate sensing, data processing, algorithmic decision-making and automated actions to coordinate and mediate social activities, and how their governance intersects with broader digital transformation.

The special issue seeks contributions examining smart systems through human-centred, behavioural and organisational perspectives. It welcomes empirical, conceptual, methodological and design-oriented papers exploring how smart systems shape conduct, allocate responsibility, structure choices and influence power dynamics, as well as how human and machine intelligence are combined and contested in various contexts.

Appel publié par Behaviour and Information Technology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Smart systems in homes, workplaces, healthcare and education
  • Smart systems in mobility, public services and platform environments
  • Human-centred AI and human-AI collaboration
  • Algorithmic decision-making and accountability
  • User adaptation, negotiation and resistance
  • AI ethics, privacy and surveillance
  • Smart and digital health technologies
  • Digital work and algorithmic management
  • Datafication, monitoring and automated feedback
  • Inclusion, exclusion and inequality
  • Smart cities and digital government
  • Comparative and cross-cultural studies

Timeline

  • October 20, 2026: Submissions accepted until
  • December 20, 2026: Manuscript deadline
